cards.title: Ten minutes with the doctor. Make them count.
cards.body: Most OPD visits are short and busy. A little prep at home means Papa's doctor spends time on the problem, not on hunting for old reports.

cards.title: Carry every medicine, not just a list
cards.body: Put the actual strips and bottles in a bag. Names on paper get misread, but the doctor can check the strip itself, including half tablets and medicines from other doctors.

cards.title: Bring recent readings and reports
cards.body: BP and sugar notes from home, the last blood test, any scans. Keep them in date order in one folder so nobody digs through a plastic bag at the counter.

cards.title: Write three questions before leaving home
cards.body: Top worry first. In the room, nerves make everyone forget. A note on your phone with three questions keeps the visit about what actually bothers Mummy.

cards.title: Last check: file, time, company
cards.body: Old prescription file, appointment slot, ID if the clinic needs it, and someone to go along if possible. Two people hear and remember more than one.

takeaway: Carry the medicines, readings, reports and three written questions, and a short visit will cover what matters.
share: Before Papa's next doctor visit: carry all medicine strips, readings, reports and three questions.
